## HIGH IMPACT

No high-impact breaking changes are confirmed from the six diffed files alone. However, one removal warrants close attention and a flag upgrade if confirmed at runtime:

### Component: `ha-list` / `ha-list-item` (Removed)

**What changed:** PR #55783 "Remove ha-list and ha-list-item" explicitly removes these two custom elements from ha-frontend.

**What LCARS rules are affected:**

The LCARS `card-mod-card-yaml` block (preamble.yaml) contains the following selectors that target these now-removed elements:

```css
ha-sortable > ha-list { … }          /* todo-list card section */
ha-check-list-item { … }             /* inside ha-list */
"ha-card ha-sortable ha-list":        /* card-mod nested selector key */
  "ha-check-list-item$": |           /* deep shadow pierce */
```

The entire to-do list card styling block depends on `ha-sortable > ha-list` as the structural wrapper. If `ha-list` is removed and replaced by `ha-list-base` (or another element), all of:
- `.header` background (`var(--lcars-card-top-color)`)
- `ha-check-list-item` row colors (`var(--active-color)`, `var(--completed-color)`)
- The card-mod nested key `"ha-card ha-sortable ha-list"` / `"ha-check-list-item$"`

…will silently fail to apply, reverting to unstyled/default HA appearance.

**Suggested fix:** Audit the new to-do card DOM structure. Replace `ha-sortable > ha-list` and `"ha-card ha-sortable ha-list"` selectors with whatever element `ha-list-base` or its replacement uses. The sibling PR #55560 "Migrate the remaining static lists to ha-list-base" and #55445 "Migrate the device, area and integration lists to ha-list-base" confirm `ha-list-base` is the replacement. Update preamble.yaml:

```yaml
# OLD
"ha-card ha-sortable ha-list":
  "ha-check-list-item$": |

# NEW (tentative — verify actual DOM)
"ha-card ha-sortable ha-list-base":
  "ha-check-list-item$": |
```

And in `card-mod-card-yaml`:
```css
/* OLD */
ha-sortable > ha-list { … }

/* NEW */
ha-sortable > ha-list-base { … }
```

## MEDIUM IMPACT

### Component: `ha-button` / `ha-icon-button` — `ariaPressed` property added

**What changed:** `ha-button.ts` gains a new `ariaPressed` property (`@property({ attribute: false })`). `ha-icon-button.ts` gains `ariaPressed: "false" | "true" | "mixed"` forwarded to the inner webawesome button via `.ariaPressed=${this.ariaPressed ?? null}`. `ha-button-toggle-group.ts` now sets `.ariaPressed` on each toggle button.

**What LCARS rules are affected:** The LCARS theme targets `ha-icon-button` extensively in `card-mod-sidebar-yaml`:

```css
div.menu {
  ha-icon-button { … }
}
@media screen and (max-width: 870px) {
  ha-button-menu > ha-icon-button { … }
  ha-icon-button { … }
}
```

And in `card-mod-root-yaml` (`div.header`):
```css
ha-button-menu > ha-icon-button { … }
ha-icon-button { … }
```

The `ariaPressed` property does not change the visual shadow DOM structure of `ha-icon-button`, but the inner webawesome `<wa-button>` now receives an `aria-pressed` attribute. If the webawesome button component applies different visual styling for `aria-pressed="true"` vs `"false"` (e.g., an accent fill or pressed indicator), toggle-group buttons and any icon buttons used as toggles may gain unexpected visual states that override or clash with LCARS palette colors.

**Suggested fix:** Inspect the webawesome `wa-button` stylesheet for `[aria-pressed="true"]` rules. If it applies a background or border change, override in the relevant `ha-icon-button$` shadow injection or via the existing `--wa-color-fill-normal` / `--wa-color-on-normal` variables already used in the edit-mode block:

```css
/* Add to card-mod-sidebar ha-icon-button or card-mod-root div.header */
ha-icon-button::part(base)[aria-pressed="true"] {
  background-color: var(--lcars-ui-tertiary);
}
```

---

### Component: Cover More-Info Dialog — Redesign (`hui-cover-more-info` / `ha-more-info-cover`)

**What changed:** PR #55614 "Redesign the cover more-info dialog" completely rebuilds the cover more-info panel. This is a shadow DOM structural overhaul.

**What LCARS rules are affected:** The LCARS `card-mod-more-info-yaml` block injects into `:host` of the more-info dialog with generic variable overrides. It does not currently pierce deeply into `ha-more-info-cover` specifically, so the CSS variable cascade (`--lcars-primary-text`, `--card-background-color`, etc.) should still apply.

However, if the redesigned cover dialog introduces new sub-elements or uses hardcoded colors (e.g., for the new tilt/slat angle controls referenced in PR #56090), those will render in HA's default palette rather than LCARS colors.

**What specifically changed:** Cover state color changed to blue (PR #56086 "Change cover state color to blue"). This sets `state-cover-*-color` variables or equivalent. LCARS does not currently define `state-cover-*-color` overrides, so this new blue will appear in the redesigned cover more-info and on any cover entity rows.

**Suggested fix:** Add cover state color overrides to `defaults.yaml` or the `&base` block:

```yaml
state-cover-open-color: var(--lcars-green)
state-cover-closed-color: var(--lcars-red)
state-cover-opening-color: var(--lcars-sunflower)
state-cover-closing-color: var(--lcars-sunflower)
```

Adjust colors to match LCARS palette preferences.

---

### Component: `ha-icon-button-prev` — `delegatesFocus` added

**What changed:** `ha-icon-button-prev.ts` adds `shadowRootOptions: { delegatesFocus: true }`. This changes focus behavior: the shadow host itself now becomes focusable, and focus delegation changes which element receives the focus ring.

**What LCARS rules are affected:** No LCARS rule currently targets `ha-icon-button-prev` or `:focus`/`:focus-within` on it directly, so the visual impact is likely minimal. However, if any card-mod CSS uses `:host(:focus)` or `:focus-visible` on adjacent selectors, the new delegation path could cause or suppress focus rings unexpectedly.

**Suggested fix:** No immediate fix required. Monitor for unintended focus-ring visibility in the sidebar (`div.menu ha-icon-button`) and header controls.

---

### Component: Camera More-Info — Layout changes

**What changed:** Multiple PRs restructure the camera more-info dialog:
- #56013 "Add a camera player with its own controls to the more info"
- #56109 "Make the camera more info as wide as its picture fits"
- #56137 "Move the camera microphone row height to its more info"

**What LCARS rules are affected:** `card-mod-more-info-yaml` applies `--lcars-primary-text`, `--card-background-color`, and `--md-sys-color-surface` to the more-info dialog host. The new camera player DOM (a new element, likely `ha-camera-player` or similar) will inherit these variables but may contain hardcoded background or sizing that creates visual mismatches (white background on a dark LCARS canvas, or controls not fitting within the LCARS color scheme).

**Suggested fix:** After updating, inspect `ha-more-info-camera` shadow DOM. Add a targeted card-mod rule if the player background or control colors break:

```yaml
card-mod-more-info-yaml: |
  "ha-more-info-camera $": |
    ha-camera-player {
      background-color: var(--lcars-background-color);
      color: var(--lcars-primary-text);
    }
```

---

### Component: Switches and Buttons — Custom theme colors

**What changed:** PR #56077 "Make switches and buttons follow custom theme colors" means `ha-switch` and button elements now consume theme color variables they previously ignored.

**What LCARS rules are affected:** LCARS defines `primary-color: var(--lcars-ui-tertiary)` and `accent-color: var(--lcars-ui-accent-color)` in `&base`. Switches that previously rendered in a hardcoded HA color will now inherit `--lcars-ui-tertiary` (currently `var(--lcars-red)`). This may cause switches to render red in the "on" state instead of the previously hardcoded HA green/teal.

**Suggested fix:** If red switches are undesirable, add explicit switch state color overrides:

```yaml
# In &base or defaults.yaml
switch-checked-color: var(--lcars-green)
# or use state-active-color which LCARS already defines
```

Alternatively, if the red-on-active is intentional LCARS behavior, no fix needed — but verify visually.
